adds.after:
- For large writebacks, use apply with `--wait` and then collect the result; it can run long. After completion, confirm final applied and skipped counts and no concurrent changes before reporting.
- Apply performs an ov write plus readback for each item and is slow, roughly 11-12 seconds per item, with embedding timeout cases up to 120 seconds; expect slow cases to move to the background.
- The apply script can shell out to the ov CLI multiple times per memory, so a 45-item batch can take a long time even when each individual call is normal.
- Large writebacks should run in the background while verification continues; do not wait idly, and do not guess or splice job ids when background execution is slow.
- Use job_list to obtain the real job id and poll until completion; if progress is slow but stable, use a blocking wait to avoid high-frequency polling overhead.
- Stdout redirection output files and job_output may only become visible when the process ends; lack of intermediate stdout is normal, so do not diagnose a hang prematurely.
- During execution, judge progress from audit-log growth rather than repeatedly reading output files that are not yet written.
- audit.jsonl appends one line per apply; its line count indicates progress, and if the path is uncertain, use just-completed apply output to identify it instead of spending time searching.
- If apply runs for many minutes with no output or appears stuck, stop repeating waits and inspect process state and the apply script logic, including network retries, interactive waits, OpenViking health, Ollama health, and the autostart skill.

- Before writeback, confirm the apply script path: it is in the project scripts directory and the working directory is D:/repository/skills.
- Before writeback, run a final privacy and sensitive-information scan on all candidate bodies; after completion, clean temporary validation scripts and keep only cache intermediates.
- Judgment result fields use judgment only as valid/invalid, note truncated to 500 characters, and reread sha verification before writeback; any body change must update the sha or readback verification fails.
- After audit writeback, run stats to obtain accurate coverage numbers; use the stats result for the coverage figure in the brief.

updates.before:
- Extract verification symbols from all technical identifiers and Chinese terms, not only backticked content; filter out session numbers, hashes, and generic words.
- Select the repository by memory type: verify tool, preference, and knowledge memories in `skills/` or the OpenViking repository; verify business memories in the corresponding business repository.
- Broad substring hits in generic symbols, aggregate repositories, and cache directories are not evidence; only exact hits in real business source code for concrete filenames, API paths, long unique identifiers, and distinctive assertions count as evidence.
- Narrow evidence checks progressively: first map project repositories and check whether referenced files and key identifiers exist, then search the whole repository for distinctive assertions such as function names, constants, APIs, CSS classes, and Chinese phrases, then filter noise such as `package-lock`, bundled artifacts, `assets`, `docs`, `e2e`, and `worktrees`, keeping only real source hits, and finally confirm the few borderline items whose core assertions do not match.
- If a core assertion appears only in memory archive copies such as `memory-migration-archive`, the referenced file does not exist anywhere, or the only support is plaintext credentials, do not treat it as valid evidence.
- If it cannot be proven with actual code or contradicts current code, classify it as INVALID.
- When exact path patterns return `files=0`, run a clean content search for distinctive tokens in real project code before invalidating; exclude `skills/`, memory archives, vector databases, cache directories, and other mirrors.
- For large batches, use one bounded verification script that checks each candidate's distinctive tokens or fixes in the actual repositories and writes compact UTF-8 evidence for staged review; avoid broad slow globs.

- For large writebacks, use apply with `--wait` and then collect the result; it can run long, so confirm final applied and skipped counts before reporting completion.
- Treat skipped=0 as the normal success condition; when skipped items have a documented URI normalization or backend limitation, report the counts and reason instead.
- Apply performs an ov write plus readback for each item and is slow, roughly 11-12 seconds per item, with embedding timeout cases up to 120 seconds; expect slow cases to move to the background.
- The apply script can shell out to the ov CLI multiple times per memory, so a 45-item batch can take a long time even when each individual call is normal.

- Use job_list to obtain the real job id and poll until completion; if progress is slow but stable, use a blocking wait to avoid high-frequency polling overhead.
- Stdout redirection output files and job_output may only become visible when the process ends; lack of intermediate stdout is normal, so do not diagnose a hang prematurely.
- During execution, judge progress from audit-log growth rather than repeatedly reading output files that are not yet written.
- audit.jsonl appends one line per apply; its line count indicates progress, and if the path is uncertain, use just-completed apply output to identify it instead of spending time searching.
- If apply runs for many minutes with no output or appears stuck, stop repeating waits and inspect process state and the apply script logic, including network retries, interactive waits, OpenViking health, Ollama health, and the autostart skill.
- Before writeback, confirm the apply script path: it is in the project scripts directory and the working directory is D:/repository/skills.
- Before writeback, run a final privacy and sensitive-information scan on all candidate bodies; after completion, clean temporary validation scripts and keep only cache intermediates.
- Judgment result fields use judgment only as valid/invalid, note truncated to 500 characters, and reread sha verification before writeback; any body change must update the sha or readback verification fails.
- If embedding errors occur because Ollama is disconnected, inspect the apply and write logic; `--wait` may block on embedding while readback verification still succeeds, so check recent audit events, recent apply output timestamps, and persisted writeback progress instead of assuming failure.
- After embedding-error writebacks, verify persisted frontmatter, including a spot check of invalid items, before reporting completion.
- If MCP health checks report healthy while OpenViking CLI writes fail during embedding, inspect service health and the autostart skill; keep collecting the running job because read, write, and reread processing may still be underway.
- Before rerunning apply after an embedding failure, do not trust green health endpoints alone: confirm the embedding model is installed, for example bge-m3-ov:latest, and that a real embed call succeeds with the expected dimension, for example /api/embed returning dim:1024.
- If Ollama embedding disconnects during apply, load the openviking-autostart skill, confirm OpenViking and Ollama are healthy, and retry; if the retried job remains stuck retrying, stop it and rerun cleanly.
- When apply readback reports skipped because a filename with spaces causes URI normalization mismatch, treat it as a normalization difference rather than a concurrent change; the memory body is unaffected and completion can still be reported.
- If a URI containing spaces is rejected by both the CLI and MCP write paths with INVALID_ARGUMENT, treat it as a genuine backend skip rather than a body-change conflict; skip it without changing or deleting the memory and still report completion.
- After apply reports skipped items, verify their current audit_status and body hash directly because an interrupted earlier run may have already written them; do not assume every skipped item failed.
- When a space-containing URI fails readback but the underscore-normalized URI shows audit_status=valid with matching body hash, note, and timestamp, report the write as successful and do not add a duplicate write.
- After apply writeback, confirm final applied and skipped counts and no concurrent changes before reporting completion.
- After audit writeback, run stats to obtain accurate coverage numbers; use the stats result for the coverage figure in the brief.
